summary: puppeteer-extra is a modular plugin framework for Puppeteer (and now Playwright via playwright-extra) that enables anti-detection through its flagship stealth plugin. The stealth plugin applies 19+ evasion techniques including navigator.webdriver deletion, chrome.runtime mocking, navigator.plugins/mimeTypes emulation, WebGL vendor spoofing, user-agent override, and --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled. It uses a dependency injection system where the StealthPlugin loads individual evasion plugins on demand. The framework works as a drop-in replacement for puppeteer/playwright - users call `puppeteer.use(StealthPlugin())` then use the standard API. Verified from code: the core PuppeteerExtra class manages plugin registration, dependency resolution, and lifecycle hooks (beforeLaunch, onPageCreated, etc.), while each evasion injects code via `page.evaluateOnNewDocument()` to patch browser fingerprinting surfaces. The playwright-extra port uses a compatibility layer to reuse puppeteer-extra plugins.

apiSurface:
Main entry points:
- `const puppeteer = require('puppeteer-extra')` - drop-in replacement
- `puppeteer.use(plugin)` - register plugin, chainable
- `puppeteer.launch(options)` - augmented launch with plugin lifecycle
- `puppeteer.connect(options)` - augmented connect
- `StealthPlugin()` - factory returning configured stealth plugin instance
- `stealthPlugin.enabledEvasions` - Set of enabled evasion names (mutable)
- `stealthPlugin.availableEvasions` - Set of all available evasion names
- `require('puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth/evasions/<name>')` - direct evasion access
Playwright: `const { chromium } = require('playwright-extra')`, `chromium.use(stealth)`, `chromium.launch()`
- `addExtra(launcher)` - create independent instance with different plugins
- `DEBUG=puppeteer-extra*,puppeteer-extra-plugin:*` for debug output
strengthsForVeridian:
- Most comprehensive stealth evasion suite available (19 techniques covering navigator, chrome, webgl, iframe, media, window objects)
- Proven track record passing major bot detection tests (at time of active development)
- Modular - can enable/disable specific evasions for compatibility
- Works with both Puppeteer and Playwright (Veridian can choose either)
- Drop-in replacement - minimal code changes to existing scraper
- Plugin architecture allows custom Veridian-specific evasions
- Active ecosystem: recaptcha, proxy, adblocker, user-data-dir plugins available
- Good TypeScript support for maintainable pipeline code
weaknessesForVeridian:
- **Abandoned**: Last commit March 2023, no updates in 2+ years. Bot detection has evolved significantly (Cloudflare, Akamai, PerimeterX, etc. all updated)
- Many evasions are Chrome-specific; Firefox/WebKit support limited
- No maintenance = no fixes for new detection vectors
- Puppeteer v9 peer dep (current is v22+) - version lock risk
- The `page.goto('about:blank')` patch for page creation is a hack that adds latency
- Some evasions (like chrome.runtime) add Chrome infobars requiring OS-level policy fixes
- No supply chain security (no SBOM, signed releases, or dependency pinning)
- Single maintainer (Markus/berstend) - bus factor of 1
- No automated testing against current bot detection services visible
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
